blocks.text: Welcome. This course gets you ready for the NCCCO Mobile Crane Operator core written exam. It's independent practice and isn't affiliated with or endorsed by the certifying body. Here's how the exam works. You get 95 multiple choice questions in 90 minutes, each with four options, and no calculator. The questions fall into four domains. Site is 22 percent. It covers ground stability, mats and cribbing, power lines during assembly, travel, and what the controlling entity owes. Operations is 28 percent. It covers leveling, load weight and radius, signals, operator aids, emergencies, dynamic and side loading, weather, and your authority to stop a lift. Technical Knowledge is 23 percent. It covers the rules and standards, terminology, inspections, rigging hardware, wire rope, and fall protection. Load Charts is 27 percent. It covers chart terms, choosing the right chart, gross and net capacity, range diagrams, parts of line, and hand arithmetic. Here's how to use the app. Practice by skill so you can work on one weak spot at a time. Review every miss and read why the right answer is right. Take timed practice exams to get used to the pace. And do the load chart drills with paper and pencil, the way you will on exam day. Tell me where you want to start.

Most people lose points in three places. The first is load charts. One problem stacks several steps: the right chart, the right work area, the next longer radius, and every deduction. Skip one and the wrong answer is waiting in the options. The second is roles. Questions often ask who is responsible, and the job titles sound alike. The third is numbers that sit close together, especially around power lines, inspections and rigging. Read every question for words like first, gross, net and except.
